summary: A double-pumped granular aluminum Bose–Hubbard dimer exploits balanced four-wave mixing to achieve parametric amplification without operating near instability, enabling sixfold bandwidth improvement at 20 dB gain while surpassing the conventional gain–bandwidth tradeoff up to 25 dB. The device maintains added noise near the quantum limit and demonstrates a 41 dB phase-sensitive gain modulation, recommending grAl as a source of pure Kerr nonlinearity for multi-pump parametric amplifiers.
motivation: Standing-wave superconducting parametric amplifiers are essential for quantum readout but face a fundamental gain–bandwidth tradeoff when operated near instability, limiting instantaneous bandwidth to tens of MHz at ∼20 dB gain needed for frequency-multiplexed qubit readout and broadband quantum optics.
method: Two simultaneous pump tones at $\omega_g = (\tilde{\omega}_a + \tilde{\omega}_b)/2$ (gain pump) and $\omega_c = \omega_g + \tilde{\omega}_a - \tilde{\omega}_b$ (conversion pump) activate two-mode squeezing, single-mode squeezing, and beam-splitter interactions in the dimer's hybridized modes; operation near the Bogoliubov point ($\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{TMS}} - \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{BS}} = -1$) provides dynamical stability by balancing competing nonlinear effects.
result: At 20 dB gain, bandwidth increases from $\sim19$ MHz (single-pump) to $\sim115$ MHz (double-pump); near-quantum-limited added noise $n_{\mathrm{add}} \approx 0.5$ photon is maintained; phase-preserving operation shows cooperative rates $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{S}} \sim 0.03$–$0.04$ with extracted Kerr coefficients $\mathcal{K}_{L,R}/(2\pi) \approx 3$ kHz in the 7 × 0.2 × 0.04 μm grAl strip.
